newsitem.title: CANADA: Methanex charge mostly for plant writedown.
newsitem.headline: Methanex charge mostly for plant writedown.

text.p: Methanex Corp said on Monday that a US$100 million after-tax fourth-quarter charge mostly covered writedowns on two methanol plants.
A company spokesman said the charge equated to about US$0.52 a share.

Chief executive Pierre Choquette told a conference call that about US$60 million of the total was to cover accounting writedowns for the company's Medicine Hat, Alberta and Waitara, New Zealand methanol plants. The remaining US$40 million would cover projected site restoration and redundancy costs. The charge "is non-cash primarily," he said.

At Medicine Hat, one of three plants will be mothballed partway through next year. It has capacity for 270,000 tonnes of methanol. The remaining two plants, which have combined capacity of 830,000 tonnes, would run around 80 percent capacity next year, the Methanex spokesman said.

When Methanex's third new plant in Chile comes onstream in 1999, production at Medicine Hat may be reduced further, he said. The plant at Waitara, New Zealand, which has capacity of 530,000 tonnes, will be idled in 1998.
Choquette said Methanex forecast its cash production costs would drop about US$5 a tonne next year.

He was unable to forecast how much costs would drop in 1998 but said it would be "nowhere near the order of magnitude" of 1997's decline. The next big drop will come in 1999 when the third Chile plant goes into production.
The company spokesman said most investors were "well prepared" for Monday's announcement.
A 0.25 drop in the company's share price to 13.50 reflected a market outlook that is "steady as she goes (for the company)...(the moves) will not have too much impact in the marketplace," he said.
